title: A radiolabeled drug tracing method to study neurotrophin-3 retention and distribution in the cochlea after nano-based local delivery
author: Lam, Gunewardene, et al.
materials: After treatment, the guinea pigs were intraperitoneally administered with a lethal dose of pentobarbitone sodium (150 mg/kg) (Lethabarb, Virbac, Australia). Transcardial perfusion and fixation was performed using 0.9% (w/v) saline (37 °C) containing 0.1% (w/v) heparin sodium and 0.025% (w/v) sodium nitrite followed by 4 °C 10% Neutral Buffered Formalin (10% NBF, Sigma, USA). The bulla was dissected out and perforated to create a small opening for cochlear inspection. The bulla was then carefully removed. Each treated cochlea, including the attached vestibular apparatus, was placed in 0.5 mL 10% NBF in a radioimmunoassay tube for gamma counting. The cochlear fluids and the implanted supraparticle remain in place and were included in the total count. Any unexpected fluid loss from the cochlea during the dissection process was captured into the same radioimmunoassay tube.

steps.title: Radiolabel NT-3 with 125I
steps.instruction: Label reconstituted human NT-3 (3–4.5 µg, PeproTech) with 0.25 mCi Na 125I (ICN Biomedicals Australasia) using the Chloramine‑T method (ProSearch International), then remove unbound radioiodine on a Biogel P6DG column and preserve the 125I‑NT‑3 in phosphate buffer containing 0.25 % (w/v) BSA and 0.1 % (w/v) sodium azide; note the specific radioactivity (46 and 46.7 µCi/µg) and incorporation efficiencies (82 % and 84 %).

substeps.instruction: Reconstitute human NT‑3 (3–4.5 µg) in appropriate buffer.
Add 0.25 mCi Na 125I and perform halogenation via the Chloramine‑T method.
Pass the reaction mixture through a Biogel P6DG chromatography column to remove unbound 125I.
Collect the eluate (125I‑NT‑3) and store it in phosphate buffer with 0.25 % (w/v) BSA and 0.1 % (w/v) sodium azide.
Record the specific radioactivity (46 and 46.7 µCi/µg) and the incorporation percentages (82 % and 84 %).

steps.title: Purify and buffer exchange 125I-NT-3
steps.instruction: Purify 125I‑NT‑3 using an Amicon Ultra‑2 3 K filtration unit pre‑coated with PBS + 1 % (w/v) BSA, perform centrifugation steps at 5500 × g, exchange into artificial perilymph (125 mM NaCl, 3.5 mM KCl, 1.3 mM CaCl₂, 25 mM NaHCO₃, 1.2 mM MgCl₂, 0.75 mM NaH₂PO₄, 5 mM glucose, pH 7.4), measure volumes and radioactivity with a Perkin Elmer WIZARD gamma counter, and adjust the final concentration to 1 µg/mL before loading into supraparticles.

substeps.instruction: Pre‑coat the Amicon Ultra‑2 3 K filter in PBS containing 1 % (w/v) BSA; incubate for 20 min.
Centrifuge the pre‑coating solution through the filter for 2 min and discard the flow‑through.
Add 1 mL of 125I‑NT‑3 to the filter and centrifuge at 5500 × g for 10 min.
Discard the ultrafiltrate.
Add artificial perilymph (125 mM NaCl, 3.5 mM KCl, 1.3 mM CaCl₂, 25 mM NaHCO₃, 1.2 mM MgCl₂, 0.75 mM NaH₂PO₄, 5 mM glucose, pH 7.4) to the filter.
Centrifuge again at 5500 × g for 10 min.
Collect the concentrated 125I‑NT‑3 solution.
Record the volumes of ultrafiltrate and concentrate.
Measure radioactivity of each fraction using a Perkin Elmer WIZARD automatic gamma counter and calculate the final 125I‑NT‑3 concentration.
Dilute or concentrate the solution to achieve 1 µg/mL of 125I‑NT‑3 for supraparticle loading.

steps.title: Euthanize, perfuse, and collect cochlea
steps.instruction: Administer a lethal intraperitoneal dose of pentobarbitone sodium (150 mg/kg, Lethabarb), perform transcardial perfusion with 0.9 % (w/v) saline at 37 °C containing 0.1 % (w/v) heparin sodium and 0.025 % (w/v) sodium nitrite followed by 4 °C 10 % Neutral Buffered Formalin, dissect the bulla, create a small opening for inspection, remove the bulla, and place each cochlea (with vestibular apparatus) in 0.5 mL 10 % NBF in a radioimmunoassay tube for gamma counting, ensuring all cochlear fluids and the implanted supraparticle remain in the tube.

substeps.instruction: Inject pentobarbitone sodium intraperitoneally at 150 mg/kg (Lethabarb, Virbac, Australia) to achieve a lethal dose.
Perform transcardial perfusion with 0.9 % (w/v) saline pre‑warmed to 37 °C containing 0.1 % (w/v) heparin sodium and 0.025 % (w/v) sodium nitrite.
Follow with perfusion of 4 °C 10 % Neutral Buffered Formalin (10 % NBF, Sigma, USA).
Dissect out the bulla and perforate it to create a small opening for cochlear inspection.
Carefully remove the bulla, keeping the cochlea and attached vestibular apparatus intact.
Transfer each treated cochlea into a radioimmunoassay tube containing 0.5 mL 10 % NBF.
Ensure that cochlear fluids and the implanted supraparticle remain in place; capture any unexpected fluid loss in the same tube.
Proceed to gamma counting of the tube.
